profile.address: near Arizona State University campus, Tempe, AZ
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged simply EdgeConneX, sits in Tempe, Arizona, and its coordinates correspond to what EdgeConneX own Phoenix market page describes as its facility located near the heart of the Arizona State University campus in Tempe, referred to elsewhere on the same page by the internal code PHX01. Per that page, the building totals 79,200 square feet with 17,300 square feet of raised floor space available for tenant racks, capable of supporting more than 600 watts per square foot and cabinet densities above 20 kilowatts. No overall megawatt figure, opening year, or named tenant is disclosed for the facility. EdgeConneX has published several network and cloud-connectivity partnership announcements tied to this Phoenix-area site, including a Phoenix-IX internet exchange node, Microsoft Azure ExpressRoute private cloud connectivity, and AWS Direct Connect availability, none of which name the facility underlying anchor tenant or tenants. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, with regional headquarters in Amsterdam and Singapore, acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020 with Sixth Street also holding a board seat, though exact ownership percentages are not disclosed on EdgeConneX own site. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, and it operates a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. The company model centers on build-to-suit and build-to-density facilities serving cloud, AI and high-performance computing, content-delivery, and network or ISP tenants. The PHX designation, shared with the undeveloped Mesa land bank referenced elsewhere on EdgeConneX own Phoenix market page, indicates this Tempe building is considered the first facility in the company Phoenix-area market numbering.
profile.research_note: 79,200 sqft total / 17,300 sqft raised floor and PHX01 designation confirmed via EdgeConneX own Phoenix market page, which locates this facility near ASU in Tempe. No MW, year-opened, or tenant disclosed.

profile.address: Elk Grove Village, IL (EdgeConneX Chicago campus)
profile.reading: EdgeConneX CHI01 sits in Elk Grove Village, Illinois, part of EdgeConneX Chicago-area campus. Per the operator own Chicago market page, CHI01 is fully occupied and carries 24 megawatts of capacity, with a facility graphic on that page labeling it Est. 2017, though that year appears only as a graphic label rather than confirmed in the page running text, so it is presented here with that caveat rather than as fully certain. No street address, square footage, or named tenant specific to CHI01 is disclosed. The same Chicago campus later expanded with CHI02, described elsewhere on the same page as a 282,000 square foot raised-floor Phase 1 building with 7 megawatts of N plus 1 capacity, and with CHI03, at 22.4 megawatts, and most recently CHI04, announced in an August 2025 press release as a more than 30 megawatt facility being built for AI-compute customer Lambda, with 23 megawatts single-tenant and service targeted for 2026, a rare instance of EdgeConneX naming a specific anchor tenant publicly. Those additional buildings are distinct from CHI01 and should not be conflated with it. EdgeConneX is a US-based edge and build-to-suit data center operator founded in 2009 and headquartered in Herndon, Virginia, acquired by EQT Infrastructure in 2020 with Sixth Street also holding a board seat. EdgeConneX describes its footprint today as more than 90 data centers across more than 60 markets in over 20 countries on four continents, operating a joint venture called AdaniConneX in India alongside a strategic investment in the China-based operator Chayora. Elk Grove Village sits in the O Hare International Airport industrial corridor northwest of downtown Chicago, an area that has become a significant data center cluster in the Midwest given its proximity to major fiber routes, the airport itself, and the interstate highway network, a pattern reflected in EdgeConneX own decision to build multiple successive facilities, CHI01 through CHI04, on essentially the same campus over time rather than scattering them across the metro area.

reading:
EdgeConneX was founded in 2009 and is headquartered at 2201 Cooperative Way in Herndon, Virginia, with regional headquarters in Schiphol-Rijk, Netherlands for EMEA and Singapore for Asia-Pacific. EQT Infrastructure, the Stockholm-based investment firm, acquired the company in 2020, providing capital for expansion into land and power acquisition.

The company's own site describes a portfolio of more than 90 facilities built or in development across five regions, Asia Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, North America, and South America, with a stated capacity range from 40 kilowatts up to 500 megawatts or more per project, spanning small edge deployments to hyperscale campuses. Notable ventures include AdaniConneX, a joint venture in India, a strategic investment in China-based Chayora, and recent expansion into Barcelona, Brussels, Israel, Indonesia, and Japan.

The registry here tracks 8 EdgeConneX facilities across five states, Arizona, California, Illinois, Michigan, and Oregon. EdgeConneX's stated 40 kilowatt to 500 megawatt project range is the widest capacity span disclosed by any operator recorded in this registry so far, reflecting a business model built around edge and regional deployments as well as large hyperscale campuses, a dual positioning distinct from the single-scale models of pure hyperscaler operators like AWS or pure metro-colocation operators like Equinix.
